title: On Eyes That Never Saw the Day
description: On Eyes That Never Saw the Day in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Edmund Butcher wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 218 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Miracles of Christ”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: On eyes that nev-er saw the day Christ pours the bright ce-les-tial ray; And deaf-ened ears, by him un-bound, Catch all the har-mo-ny of sound.

lines: On eyes that never saw the day
Christ pours the bright celestial ray;
And deafened ears, by him unbound,
Catch all the harmony of sound.
Lameness takes up its bed, and goes
Rejoicing in the strength that flows
Through every nerve; and, free from pain,
Pours forth to God the grateful strain.
The shattered mind his word restores,
And tunes afresh the mental powers;
The dead revive, to life return,
And bid affection cease to mourn.
Canst thou, my soul, these wonders trace,
Canst thou behold thy Prophet's power,
And not the God he served adore?

licence: Public domain: Edmund Butcher died in 1822.
credits: Words by Edmund Butcher (1757–1822), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
